headline: US electronics factory prices jump 12.9%, fastest in the series
text:
# US electronics factory prices jump 12.9%, fastest in the series

Chip-era price pressure in America, record electricity bills in Austria and Luxembourg, and a collapse in Austrian pharma output make today's page one about supply, not demand.

## Today in the data

### US electronics prices break their range
[US factory-gate prices, computers and electronics, vs chip output](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
US producer prices for computer and electronic products rose 12.9% in the year to Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors, index 120.0), against a typical +0.63%. Note how flat the yoy line is before 2025: this sector normally deflates. Worth checking against semiconductor output, up 11.9% in Jul 2026 (us-chips); the BLS index is not seasonally adjusted and base periods differ by series.

### Austrian and Luxembourg power bills at records
[Household electricity prices, Austria and Luxembourg, EUR/kWh](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austrian households paid €0.3272/kWh in H2 2025, up 34.3% on a year earlier, the largest rise since 2008; Luxembourg was €0.2665, up 31.7% (energy-household-eu). The two lines turn up together after a 2024 dip. Prices include all taxes and levies, so the withdrawal of a subsidy shows up as a price rise: a base effect against a capped 2024 is the first thing to rule out.

### Austrian pharma output halves
[Austria: pharmaceutical and chemical production, 2021=100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austrian pharma production (C21) was 160.4 in Jul 2026, down 45.7% on a year earlier — the sharpest fall in the series (eu-ipi-sectors). Chemicals (C20) sat at 92.7 and did nothing similar, so this is a pharma-specific swing. Pharma indices are plant-lumpy and heavily revised; treat one month as provisional.

### Hungarian mining doubles in a year
[Hungary: mining and quarrying output, 2021=100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Hungarian mining and quarrying reached 155.7 in Jul 2026, up 101.9% on the year, the biggest rise since Sep 2018 (eu-mining-ipi). The chart shows a small, jumpy index: swings of this size recur roughly every few years. The low 2025 base (77.1) does much of the work.

### Britain's coal power all but gone
[UK electricity: coal, gas and wind, TWh a year](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
UK coal generation was 0.33 TWh in 2025, down 82.6% on 2024, the sharpest fall in a record beginning in 1921 (electricity-mix). Wind supplied 85.8 TWh and gas 90.9 TWh the same year — the crossover is nearly complete. The latest year is often Ember's provisional figure.

### Estonia's new-car market halves
[Estonia: new car registrations by fuel](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Estonia registered 13,141 new cars in 2025, down 49.0% on 2024, with diesel down 70.4% to 1,738 (eu-car-registrations). Battery-electric registrations, 872, fell with the rest rather than taking share. Worth checking against the 2025 car tax; the series only starts in 2014, so "record" means twelve comparisons.

### Egypt's FDI gives back last year's surge
[Egypt: net FDI inflows, current US dollars](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Egyptian net FDI inflows were $15.45bn in 2025, $31.1bn below 2024, the sharpest fall since the record began in 1971 (macro-external). The chart shows 2024 as a single spike well outside the historical range, so the fall is mostly its reversal. World Bank annual data lags and is revised.

## Forecasts

### US electronics PPI keeps climbing into autumn
[us-ppi-sectors:computer_electronic: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 120.05 in Aug 2026 (us-ppi-sectors). The tool chose Holt-Winters additive with a 12-month season; in-sample MAPE is 0.28%. It puts November 2026 at 122.33, with a 95% band of 120.90 to 123.77. The band is only the spread of past one-step errors scaled up with the horizon, so it assumes the current trend continues. A tariff change, or a break in the chip cycle, would take the outcome outside it.

### Austrian bills drift sideways near the record
[energy-household-eu:AT: Holt-Winters forecast, 2 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austria last printed €0.3272/kWh in H2 2025 (energy-household-eu). Holt-Winters, period 2, in-sample MAPE 3.3%, projects €0.3249 for H2 2026 with a band of €0.2904 to €0.3594. The band says the model's past errors would leave the price anywhere between last year's level and a further 10% rise. This is a taxed, partly administered price: the projection extrapolates its past, not policy. A new levy or a network-tariff decision would move it outside the band.

### Hungarian mining holds near its new high
[eu-mining-ipi:HU|B: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last reading is 155.7 in Jul 2026 (eu-mining-ipi). Holt-Winters additive, period 12, fits poorly by the standards of this page: in-sample MAPE 9.2%. October 2026 is projected at 157.7 with a band of 118.1 to 197.3 — wide because the series itself jumps. The band reflects that volatility, nothing more. A single quarry or field going offline would settle it either way.

## Correlations

- **Austria vs Luxembourg household electricity** (yoy, 2008-S2 to 2025-S2, n=35): r = 0.61 at lag −1 and 0.53 contemporaneous, clears the band. The two markets re-price together within a half-year, consistent with a common wholesale and tax-cycle driver rather than one country leading.
- **US semiconductor output vs electronics PPI** (yoy, 2012-01 to 2026-07, n=175): r = 0.07 at lag 0, strongest |r| just 0.14, not distinguishable from zero. Volume and price in this sector move on separate clocks, so today's price jump is not simply an output story.

## What to watch

- **us-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-08): the September print says whether 12.9% was a peak or a step.
- **eu-ipi-sectors** (last 2026-07): August settles whether Austria's C21 collapse is a one-month plant effect.
- **eu-mining-ipi** (last 2026-07): August shows if Hungary's doubling holds above 150.
- **eu-hicp** and **cpi-eu** (last 2026-07): the consumer side of the European electricity rise.
- **cattle-parity, cattle-tr, eu-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-08): next in the queue after today's producer-price story.

## Sources

- us-ppi-sectors — BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly; last 2026-08.
- us-chips — Federal Reserve industrial production via FRED, NAICS 3344 and 334, monthly; last 2026-07.
- energy-household-eu — Eurostat nrg_pc_204, band DC, all taxes included; last 2025-S2.
- eu-ipi-sectors — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, 2021=100, monthly; last 2026-07.
- eu-mining-ipi — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, mining and quarrying, 2021=100; last 2026-07.
- electricity-mix — Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute via Our World in Data; last 2025.
- eu-car-registrations — Eurostat road_eqr_carpda; last 2025.
- macro-external — World Bank World Development Indicators; last 2025.
